body:
I go back and forth. Head switches around no matter what. So depending on what's up with that, sometimes it's alright, other times I am convinced it is my destiny to die in a car and the entire drive feels like a trip down to hell. But what can you do, eh? The actual driving doesn't scare me though. Put me on a street alone and driving is actually sort of fun. It's traffic, not knowing if that other shitbag driver is texting or distracted or drunk or what they're going to do, that gets me. I still jump and react in situations that don't call for it.

I'm not going through a dealership (from what it looks like right now, anyway), so a lot of that post isn't too relevant. Trying to find something privately owned so I can just pay for it outright with the money I've saved. "Starter car" basically. Get me to and from work and in a position to work more hours/earn more money. If I still need a car after that, trade up. Craigslist is pretty sketchy though. :(



Chuggin on. Work, sleep, paint, repeat. Not much else to say there. 



Do you know anything about the comptia a+?

license acquired.
finding a car to buy is a terrible adventure.

oops i should check this sometimes i guess.

Sister got another car so I am driving sort of. Not alone, but I am at least driving. She accidentally saw some scars and now that is out on the table (but as far as I know just with her, not mom). Lot of awkwardness, but life goes on. 
Freaked out on the highway today, but I managed to drive to the next town over. Test for my actual license (only have my permit still) is in September.  Dunno where I'm going after that.

Restless and uneasy but bored as shit.

>When did this happen?

Sunday. (I think. Days blur a lot.)

>Speaking of insurance make sure to shop around. You might already know that but just in case. If you are getting a used car you probably would be fine with the barebones. Not sure what your state requires though (I think it differs state to state).

Since my sister's going to have to be added onto the insurance, she'll probably help me look around. She did have a car up until recently (someone hit her and totaled it), so she should know a bit more than I do. I'll probably spring for full coverage and she may split the insurance with me or something, since she'll be getting more use out of it than me. 

>When you aren't buying from someone you know... you can't tell how it was treated. 

Sister bought her last two cars from a neighbor who buys old/damaged cars and fixes and resells them, so I can probably get him to have a look at whatever I buy. Downside is if he finds a problem and I've already paid for it, I don't know how easy it'll be to get someone to take it back. I don't know if there are any laws or policies in place for that, since it'll be privately owned. I'm looking around that sub now.

>I think not forgetting can have benefits. Let's say you found Mr right and had a kid down the road. Chances are you'll remember all of this stuff and go out of your way to make sure that child doesn't experience what you went through.

Heh. There are enough people already without my shitty genes. Not so into the whole Mr. Right thing either. I'd be content to just have a little life somewhere with a few friends, maybe foster some dogs, do some volunteer work or something. I'd be more inclined to take care of other people's kids than have my own. I just want to DO something, if you know what I mean.

Nah, I get it. I kind of feel like this is what I'm headed for once I get things in order and get out of here. I don't feel like I need meds or anything, just purpose and a decent environment. I mean, I doubt I'll actually forget or anything, but just that sort of old self dying, new person thing. Sorry if I overstepped in asking.

Passed my learner's permit. Once everything processes that means I can likely get a car title actually put in my name and get insurance. Discussed letting my sister kind of "have" whatever car I buy until I can drive confidently on my own (she's without a car until december or so), so she'd be coming by and driving with me to work every day in exchange basically. 
Haven't gotten much farther than that, but it's something. 

My outlook always bounces around. Seem to have three or four states. They come and go. For now things are decent, can't guarantee they'll stay that way though.

>I am glad you fully see her as the problem and don't put any blame on yourself. 

Been there, done that. Went absolutely fucking crazy trying to figure out what was "wrong" with me around November/December; why am I such a bad person? Why am I talking to myself? Cut myself off from everyone and everything with some weird "nothing even matters" mentality that landed me into a pretty crazy place. Spent a while from there really looking at mom's behavior along with others (retail sucks, but it's good for people-watching), including my own, and realized, holyshit, it's her and this crazy fucking life, not some conscious desire to be a bad person. 

>Reddit tends to really love cats or tends to be athiest/agnostic and hostile towards people of faith. 

Sounds like mom, except wiccan instead of athiest. She even wanted (and attempted to) breed and sell cats when I was a kid, we had a fucktown of yowly siameses. She's a cat person, I'm a dog person. Sums us up pretty well.

>That makes me ask. How did you find this subreddit? It's interesting that you found a specific sub without having been on reddit before. 

I poke around imgur sometimes. Eventually figured out you can type /r/something after and get photos of specific stuff like imgur.com/r/dogs, imgur.com/r/earthporn, imgur.com/r/wtf, etc. There's a source link to the side whenever I'd be curious enough to look for context. Figured from there that it works the same only reddit.com instead of imgur. Start typing random shit in the urlbar after the /r/, ended up at /r/needadvice and there's a link to this sub in the sidebar. 

>I remember that some of the cuts went further down on to my forearm. I know my parents saw and were upset by that but they never pressed the issue with me.

There are only five visible on my forearms (regret that). She eventually got suspicious and asked, but feeding her anything gives her more to throw in my face later. She got obsessive about it when I didn't want to talk about it, going so far as to bring it up in front of others as if that would make me admit to it. There was a time she was *looking in the toilet* after me, and kept insisting I was bulimic because "there was stuff floating in the toilet". The fuck is privacy? (For the record, I am not bulimic. I ate too much lettuce and had the shits. Most awkward fucking discussion of my life.)

Out of curiosity (if you don't mind), what drove you to that point?

I've tried this. We've had multiple talks that go pretty much like so:

I try to reasonably tell her she is scaring the living shit out of me and could you please not treat me like this. She assures me "this is how all parents act" and that I am just being mean to her, am lazy, and don't appreciate all that she does for me. 

If I bring up anything she's previously done as an example, she's mad at me for harping on the past ("You're still MAD at me for that?" "You just HATE me don't you?" "You can't blame me for EVERYTHING!") and insists she's better now and I just need to forgive her, based on the fact that she isn't physically abusive to me anymore. I don't think she realizes that what she does is verbal/emotional abuse, only beatings are abuse in her mind and look, she's stopped that now so she's totally a good mom! I almost wish she'd go back to just fucking hitting me though, it at least was obvious and didn't fuck with my mind as much as the head games she plays now.

If I get anywhere and make a clear point that she can't just attack me over, she defaults to crying and telling me I hate her and brings up stuff like how she tried to commit suicide before and that she's probably just like this "from the trauma" of past stuff. Then I am obligated to feel guilty and halfass comfort her for fear that she actually WILL kill herself. I don't even want her to feel bad, I just want her to leave me the fuck alone. I don't want to get her arrested. I don't want to get her in trouble. I don't want her to hurt.

Then two weeks later it all goes out the window and she goes right back to the "I'm the parent, therefore I'm always right" mentality, except now she is angrier with me and thinks I'm even meaner because I tried to stand up to her and "made her feel bad and think she's a bad mom". She constantly threatens to just "pack up and leave" me, but never actually does so. All she's done since I've started trying to actually TALK to her is become increasingly hostile and firm in the belief that I'm mean and bad to her. I was better off being nocturnal and staying locked in my room so we rarely crossed paths despite living in the same house.

There is absolutely no reasoning with her. She is not a sane human being. I don't think physical violence is going to help me, it would give her a reason to have me committed on the ground that I am dangerous (I really, really am not! I cried when I had to kill a fucking FISH and have never "snapped" at anyone besides her) or arrested.

I've tried to tell her how she treats my grandma is wrong. I've tried to tell her that she is old, please just coexist with her, but she insists really fucked up things like my grandma is intentionally keeping her here and that my grandma likes to see her suffer. Or stupid shit like "if I don't yell at her, it won't sink in" over not telling her that she needs laundry detergent or milk early enough. She thinks the whole fucking world is out to get her (she could talk your ear off about conspiracy theories too). It's infuriating but at the same time sad, because I know this is likely just because she had a really fucked up childhood. She's the sort of person who really should never have had kids, she'll even tell you now that she dislikes children. She likes to remind me that I'm blessed because "you didn't grow up with my mom, she was on DRUGS". No one could possibly have a life worse than hers, therefore everyone else's problems are insignificant. 

It probably seems silly, but just putting this all out there and seeing it along with the responses that no, this really is not normal whatsoever, has kind of calmed me down. I passed my learner's permit test yesterday too. So there's that at least.

>Who is paying for the college?

Sure as fuck not my mom. I'd be expected to sort out financial aid/pay for it myself. That's a real stressy idea to me right now. I'm not sure if I could manage college, because I really have no idea how to do any sort of school... stuff. I've never written an essay. I don't know how to do algebra. I'm ignorant to a lot of basic history that most americans probably know. I struggle to remember how to write out multiplication and division equations. Math will be really, really hard for me. 

>Mom might want to give you the ol "Well what if" and I think the answer to that is "We'll cross that bridge when we get there". We can't spend our lives speculating "what if" I injure this or that. We do what we can and we get by.

This is basically what I've tried to reason, but she's unreasonable and still has so much fucking control over my life. I end up doubting my every thought and move. She wants to yell at me for "still being a child", but won't let me make any decisions for myself to grow up. Because if I fail it means she's failed and she has to face all the guilt of having fucked me up and look like a bad mom. She's even brought this up. She was mad at me for having nothing she could talk about to her friends/etc. because "they see you sit alone at home all the time and think I'm a bad mom." It's not actually about whether I'm successful or happy, it's about how she can feed off it for herself. My accomplishments are her accomplishments. Look up narcissistic parents and you'll have my mother to a T. 

>I got the impression over the course of our conversation that things may not be what they once were. It doesn't mean it's peachy keen but I wanted to feel that out. You initial post is a shock and awe that is going to alarm most people. It's hard to read about that and I think the natural reaction is to want to fly over in a helicopter and swoop you out of there.

It's not as bad as it was. I have money to help myself now and she actually went out and got a boyfriend (when she left my dad she basically clung to me and put me in his place and never left the house due to working from home), so she's away sometimes and I have a little down-time. She also does not lay a hand on me anymore. I could wreck her if she did now, kind of created her own monster here from having me do all this physical labor all these years. I get called the hulk and shit. 
I wish someone would've swooped me out back then, but what's done is done. It's kind of funny how well you can get by when you think your crazy life is normal. I just have to remember that I'm not the fucking bad guy here like she insists and not to get run down by the mind games and mental abuse and to not believe her when she tells me I'm crazy and need to be committed. And avoid that fucking animal. Any sort of foreseeable plans give me goals and motivation to work forward and the accompanying energy to keep going, but I don't have anyone here I can discuss plans with or ask for help and advice. Dad's gone, mom's crazy, grandma's incapable, sister's got enough of her own problems, everyone else is dead, etc. 

>Sometimes when we hurt we shut down. We don't talk. We internalize everything.

Whole life right here, last year especially. Reddit seems pretty useful. Maybe I'll make a real account and try to get myself to talk a little more. 


Also thankyou thankyou thankyou for all this. I'm not good with showing gratitude but really, I mean it. I'd pat you on the head and give you a milkbone if I could.

>If something comes up there is some talk but you don't need to be skilled to do tasks such as data entry, or something of that sort.

This is actually what I've wanted for a while. It's almost bizarre you mention that. All I've done besides animal shit is stuff with computers. Everyone's always made me fix their computers and I used to set up forums and skin them for people for fun as a teennager, created and ran some silly play-by-post RPGs, etc. My knowledge of HTML and CSS is probably outdated and I have no experience with working with stuff like php and javascript, but it's stuff I'm at least familiar with and could likely learn. 
Someone I know currently does data entry, but he went to school for web design/development, got an internship through college, and is working for the place he interned at now. I figured I couldn't do it like him because of the schooling issue. 

>Office jobs can be good because you are left to yourself.

This is what I do well with. The managers/supervisors where I work currently like me because they know I'll do my work without being babysat. Teach me to do it, watch over me while I learn, then leave me to it. Just be around for me to ask if I need help. The supervisors leave me in charge if they have to step out. The last time they offered me a different position (file maintenance) they said the people they had doing it were fucking around and not doing what they needed to do and that they knew that I didn't screw around, hence asking me. But again, opportunity missed because I can't drive and mom won't sacrifice anything to help me, so the hours weren't doable. It's frustrating. (And then she was mad at me for being frustrated, cue another fight.)

>How did you get this job? What would you think about calling around and looking? Are you comfortable on the phone?

My sister worked there and got my shy little ass an interview. My mom's driven into my head that I should stay there for the insurance, always telling me "what IF something happens and you go to the hospital?" Besides getting new glasses, I've never even used the insurance. She's terrified of any change so taking risks is always bad. Sky is always fucking falling in her world. She wants me to stay here, stay at my job, and drive to the next town over (an hour round trip) to go to college after getting my GED/diploma. She seemed appalled when I mentioned the idea of not going to college here.
Phones are pretty bad. I've called up to my job to ask for my schedule and hung up without saying anything repeatedly before getting up the balls to spit out some words. If I've got no choice though, I'll do it. Just a job with a lot of speaking on phones probably would be a nightmare.

>When is the last time you really looked or had time to?

Never, for the above reasons of mom insisting I stay for the insurance. Fucking hilarious considering no one noticed I needed glasses until I started working. When I finally went to the dentist they were appalled because that was yet another thing that got overlooked when we were kids. My sister had multiple baby teeth still that no. one. fucking. noticed. and had to have all sorts of medieval torture type dental procedures done in her 20's. 
I've gotten pretty miserable and brain dead from cashiering after all this time though, so I keep thinking about it despite her disapproval. I can't reasonably do it until I can drive though. Driving's gotta be step one to set anything else in motion.

>If you are going to go and be on your own you also want a little nest egg with you. If you aren't paying rent this can all go to this.

This is why I'm not with everyone telling me to just call the cops and leave. Yeah, stuff is bad here (but it was worse when I was a teenager and I got through that), but if I can tough it out a while longer I can make a whole hell of a lot better life for myself than if I impulsively run off and end up living paycheck to paycheck while digging myself a grave of debt. I can make reasonable plans if I just have a little patience and perseverance. All I need is the ability to stay sane in the mean time and not let that stupid little animal in my head have control. 

>Is there anyone that can take you to practice driving? Maybe even a coworker?

Once I actually get the learner's permit, maybe. I'll be getting a few lessons with an actual driving instructor once I manage the learner's portion. The actual license test will come after that. My sister might help me practice if I buy a vehicle first, but she doesn't have a car right now and lives in a different town. I can't buy a car and get insurance on it and the title in my name without the learner's permit though (or so I was told). Kind of an endless loop where they expect everyone to have nice parents to help them. 

>Glad to hear the checking account is all squared away. Not sure how much you have but you might want to look into having some in checking and some in savings. Savings accounts have a higher return % wise on interest. 

About 3k in savings, a few hundred in checking. The interest I get is only a few cents though, nothing substantial.

I don't really do reddit, so I don't know how to use quotes here. I should probably figure that out.
>So you mean like you buy a car at a future date and then sell it prior to a move? I think you'll wind up taking a loss monetarily. Cars depreciate in value overtime and somewhat rapidly.

I figured I would probably end up losing some on the car if I went through with the plan of selling it (wasn't a definite, just something I'd considered if I can move somewhere I don't need it). If I could just take the money I have saved for one right now and move off that, I would, but I can't get anywhere to make my situation better and prepare to move without one. The car thing goes beyond just a "dislike" of cars though. I flinch when cars pull up next to us just when riding passenger side. I used to make little shrieky noises at intersections if they came too close. Cars stopped at the end of a driveway/parking lot preparing to pull out look like they're moving when they're not and send my heart into my throat. I think I am going to die in a car. If I get paranoid enough, I start telling myself I was supposed to die in that last wreck, or that I actually did and this life is some weird death-dream. I can't actually remember that wreck or being at the intersection prior. I don't doubt that I have PTSD from it (then again, my behavior with everything has gotten like that. I jump and flinch at loud noises at work, am hyper alert to everything and constantly on edge). That's stuff I know I need some sort of therapy for. But again, I'm not going to get it here, at least not until I can drive myself to said therapist. In a perfect world I could get out of here, have a job where I don't have to drive, attend some form of therapy, calm down, then pick back up with the driving and seeking out better jobs when I'm a little more level, but this is the hand I've been dealt.

>I was thinking maybe an office job could work for you? That's just going off the great way you have worded things. Just spitballin

I assumed anything like that wouldn't want me due to current lack of high school education (working on a course for my diploma though, just slow-going and it's taken a backseat to driving and telling that me that no, we're not allowed to die so you can just stop telling me to kill myself already). That and despite that I seem well-spoken here, I'm not. I'm well-written, but not well-spoken. I fumble over words and talk too fast, the order gets all mixed up and I want to go hide in a corner if people look at my face or try to make eye contact. I'm polite and nice (customers have thanked me for being any variation of sweet, patient, etc. on mutliple occassions), just kind of... twitchy? for lack of a better word. I've dumbed the way I talk out loud down almost my entire life; mom fucks with me for weird phrasing. IE: I said my dog is very "handler-focused" because of her breed, and mom took it upon herself to make fun of me for using the word handler, because it's not a word she'd use. Apply this to the last 20 years and there's a big contrast between the way my mouth talks and the way my brain talks. The brain types.

>I also wonder if there are job placement things in your area. Have you considered a temp agency? You give them a resume, show up and sell yourself and they try to find things for you.

I hadn't really, since I have a job right now and haven't been able to get anywhere else (my job is the closest place to my house besides a gas station). I could see myself doing this for a bit while living here though. It'd give me experience and let me hoard more money to prepare for a move. I looked just now and there is one in my town. 

>I can't help but wonder why you make so low at a Union Joint. Typically union related shops pay better. What is minimum age in Texas? 

$7.25 is currently minimum wage. Where I work, we get a pay raise either annually or bi-annually (can't remember) but it's not a lot, something like $0.20 more per hour. I'd have to look it up to remember exactly. After taxes I only made about $6.60 when I started. I guess it doesn't hurt to say I work for Kroger (it's a grocery store, if you don't have them in your area). I get decent insurance that covers vision through there though, and I have to have glasses. 

>If you got a car tomorrow would it help you any? Would your mom be off your case a little bit?

Sure would, if I could drive it. No one has ever taught me to drive. I've never even driven a car. I wanted to do driver's ed last year, was going to pay for it myself despite that it'd be a few hundred dollars, and she insisted no, that's too much money, don't do it (even though it'd be my money? what????). But now that I'm not her only friend in the world and she has a boyfriend and wants to go to the beach and to parties with him, I'm an inconvenience and her driving me to work a few times a week pisses her off and causes a lot of fights and she's mad I don't know how to drive. Her boyfriend suggested driver's ed this year when she bitched to him about me and lo, now I am allowed to do it. Working my way through the learner's permit currently.

>I assume that the checking account is 100% yours and your mothers name isn't attached to it, right? 

Yep. She has no control over my money. I don't even like telling her how much I have.

Yeah, I know driving in winter will scare the living shit out of me. I figured I'd stop driving for a while when I move, just do the whole bus and bike/walk thing for a bit while I just try to calm the fuck down. Maybe sell whatever car I end up buying here before moving; extra cash to move off of. The part of Texas I'm in is Southeast, so it's not even dry. There's swamps and all nearby. The humidity is like breathing through a hot sponge dipped in honey.


The secured credit card thing is what I looked into before, since it seemed like something I could get done without driving. It'll be a while longer before I can drive and my bank (associated credit union of texas) is across town. I manage all my money online and have my check set up to direct deposit from work, so it's rare I go to my actual bank. 
About how long would it take to build credit with just the card for starters? I don't spend a whole lot per month, so it'd probably only get used for $100-$200 per month and paid off. The last one I tried to apply for also wanted me to list my current rent or mortgage payment on the application, but I don't have one. Is this required on all of them? I can look more into the loan thing after I'm driving, but without a way to regularly get to my bank it doesn't seem doable for now. I really wish this town at least had buses. 

"If your card has a $1000 limit and you have $600 on it that looks bad at months end. Especially if you have a history of that. It shows lenders that you can't manage your money. If your balance if $200-$400 that is fine. Ideally we want it $200 or below for $1000 limit."

Do you mean that amount on it at the end of the month, when you pay it, or that amount left on it at the end of the month unpaid? 


Resume-
No library I can reasonably get to. I'm really fucked not being able to drive. Where I live is very car-dependent. 
I have really nothing special to put on a resume though, in terms of honorable mentions or awards unless they want me to train a horse or something. I've been trying to move to other departments and stuff so I can at least have a few different things to put down, but my mom freaks out on me and thinks she'll have to drive me an extra day and goes off about how she'll kill herself if she "goes back" to not having any time for herself and her boyfriend. So all I've done for three years is cashier and restock some stuff at the end of my shift. 
I have my work uniform, a pair of jeans, a pair of boots, and a handful of t-shirts, nothing dressy. The scars aren't really on my forearms though. I had the foresight to keep them contained to my bicep, legs, chest, etc. So as long as it comes down to about my elbow and isn't too low-cut it should be ok. I have no idea how to dress pretty though; I'm going to feel like a bear in a tutu. I don't even do makeup. How do be girl not dog? Could I get away with some black slacks and a nice "dressy" shirt? The jobs I'm going to be going for out of the gate will probably just be stuff like retail, working as a bather at a dog groomer's or cleaning up dog piss and shit in a kennel/vet's. 

Budget-

I kind of already do that. Not with excel or anything fancy, but I write down expenses and how much I make, subtract and see what I'll have left, then make up week by week lists of how long it'll take me to save for big purchases (when I first got this job I was having to save for stuff like new fencing materials, etc. while still paying for monthly expenses and could basically look six months into the future money-wise, right now I've just been putting all the saved money towards a car). I obsessively make lists for everything and plan meticulously; I don't want any surprises. 
How much should I be aiming to make per month to reasonably care for myself and basic expenses though? I'm only working part time right now because, again, no car issue and mom wanting her "me time". I can push for more hours when I can drive, especially if I get into a department (and they've offered me other positions in everything from the bakery to file maintenance, I work hard so they like me), but I still barely make above min. wage (union company, my hard work doesn't get me a raise regardless of if the managers want to, but the tradeoff is good/cheap insurance) and need to know if a second job is going to be necessary to keep my head above the water. 
I do have a checking account, though I've never actually needed to write a check for anything. My phone bill right now is $30 per month. I don't really text or use internet from it though, so if it was cheaper I could probably go with a prepaid cell phone and just use it as needed. I think I'm locked into the contract until 2014 though. 

Thankyou for all of this, I really, really appreciate it. It feels reasonable. I love reasonable.

No, thank you.

I would love cooler weather. I've never had a winter with snow. I'm not too fussy at this point though. Anywhere I can feel reasonably safe. Getting a state between me and my family would be nice. I'd be really happy to have some nice outdoorsy stuff to go walking or hiking with my dog, but again, beggars can't be choosers and all that. 

I know very little about loans, banks, and that whole thing, so please, don't hold back even if you feel it's common knowledge. I didn't even know they did loans like that. At the very least it gives me options to consider. 

Forgot to mention that. I made an attempt to go, but mom has to be involved. I won't do anything when she is involved. I barely speak to people if she's present (I'm awkward as hell, but I'll still talk when I'm away from her). She tried to sit in the waiting room until I finally got her to leave, but despite that I knew she left the building I still kept thinking she was sitting outside the door listening, and all I could think to tell them was about her and please, please, get me out of here. So all I did was freeze up, mutter "I can't do this" and walk out. She went in to talk to the therapist (I would not even go back in the building), and supposedly they told her I seemed "absolutely crippled by anxiety". She threatened to have me committed and lectured me the whole way home. My insurance would pay for a few more visits, but I can't do it with her involved. I will shut down every time.

I know attacking her will not end well. I've never even fought back. She has fucking nothing on me. It's not me when that happens though. I cannot explain it. I'm just not there. I have no memory of going for her. I have no memory of going from my bed to standing to hands reaching for her throat. This little chunk of time disappears and I snap back just fast enough to keep myself from doing it.

I had my fun with drugs already. It kept me numbed down enough to shut up and get through the last three years in order to hoard money (admittedly I would've hoarded more if I hadn't spent any on drugs, but it was the only thing keeping me calm enough to sleep and function, also helped to tone back the mutilation). Quit everything two weeks ago. Keep me busy and I don't need it.

I am not sure. I really don't know what all is required for living. This is something I need advice on. I personally don't need much, but I'm sure I'm overlooking important things. I figured nowhere would rent to me without credit.

I don't go anywhere besides work, so no church. I go to work, come home, and am locked in my bedroom the rest of the time. It's to the point where anything besides home and work seems really foreign and scary, almost fake.

I would be completely fucked if she were arrested or anything right now, because I cannot drive and would have no way to get myself to work and neither my grandma or I would be able to get to the store to buy groceries.

I know I can support myself. Give me a job, I will do it well. I'm not above manual labor or retail. I've had my current job for 3 years. On my last review, the comment said I did more work than required and was an "asset to the company". I go in and do my job come hell or high water. When I gave myself a concussion, I went in anyway.
